senses.definition: harmful or unfavorable
senses.example: The drug was withdrawn after reports of adverse side effects.

words.note: Adverse describes conditions or effects; averse describes a person's reluctance, as in "averse to risk."

senses.definition: friendly, good-natured and easy to talk to
senses.example: The affable librarian knew every regular by name.

senses.definition: distant and uninvolved, not friendly
senses.example: New colleagues found him aloof until they learned he was simply shy.

senses.definition: having a friendly and pleasant manner
senses.example: The talks stayed amiable even when the two sides disagreed.

senses.definition: something that deviates from what is standard or expected
senses.example: A warm week in January is an anomaly, not proof of a trend.

senses.definition: anxious or fearful that something bad will happen
senses.example: She was apprehensive about driving in the snow.

senses.definition: very enthusiastic or passionate
senses.example: An ardent fan, he hadn't missed a home game in ten years.

senses.definition: to make an unpleasant feeling less intense
senses.example: A long talk with her sister assuaged her fears about the surgery.

senses.definition: to satisfy an appetite or desire
senses.example: Nothing could assuage his curiosity about the locked room.

senses.definition: having the ability to assess situations accurately and turn them to one's advantage
senses.example: An astute investor, she sold her shares just before the crash.

senses.definition: showing a willingness to take bold risks
senses.example: The climbers made an audacious attempt on the north face in winter.

senses.definition: showing impudent lack of respect
senses.example: It was audacious of him to ask for a raise on his first day.

senses.definition: the right or condition of self-government; independence
senses.example: The region was granted autonomy over its schools and courts.

senses.definition: so lacking in originality as to be obvious and boring
senses.example: The speech was a string of banal remarks about teamwork.

senses.definition: well-meaning and kindly
senses.example: A benevolent neighbor paid for the repairs without being asked.

senses.definition: to express severe, often formal, disapproval of
senses.example: The senator was censured for misusing campaign funds.

senses.definition: the formal expression of severe disapproval
senses.example: The minister faced censure from her own party.

senses.definition: wary and unwilling to take risks; cautious
senses.example: Investors became circumspect after the bank's collapse.

senses.definition: to confirm or give support to a statement or theory
senses.example: Two witnesses corroborated the driver's account of the accident.

senses.definition: to expose the falseness of an idea or belief
senses.example: The article debunks the myth that we use only ten percent of our brains.

senses.definition: intended to teach, particularly in having moral instruction as an ulterior motive
senses.example: The children's book was charming but a little too didactic.

senses.definition: to perceive or recognize something, often with difficulty
senses.example: In the fog we could barely discern the outline of the hills.

senses.definition: to distinguish one thing from another; to judge well
senses.example: It takes experience to discern good advice from bad.

senses.definition: outstandingly bad; shocking
senses.example: The referee's call was an egregious error.

senses.definition: a person or thing that is mysterious or difficult to understand
senses.example: Despite years of research, the stone circle remains an enigma.

senses.definition: the state or feeling of being actively opposed or hostile to someone
senses.example: The old enmity between the families flared up again at the wedding.

senses.definition: having or showing great knowledge or learning
senses.example: The erudite lecture covered three thousand years of history.

senses.definition: to make a problem, bad situation or negative feeling worse
senses.example: Cutting the bus service only exacerbated the traffic problem.

senses.definition: to absolve someone from blame for a fault or wrongdoing
senses.example: DNA evidence exonerated the man after ten years in prison.

senses.definition: excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters
senses.example: The garrulous passenger talked for the entire flight.

senses.definition: fond of company; sociable
senses.example: Gregarious by nature, she knew everyone in the building.

senses.definition: (of animals) living in flocks or colonies
senses.example: Starlings are gregarious birds that roost by the thousands.

senses.definition: sly or cunning intelligence
senses.example: The fox in the fable uses guile rather than strength.

senses.definition: unable to be affected by
senses.example: She seemed impervious to criticism.

senses.definition: not allowing fluid to pass through
senses.example: The jacket is made of an impervious fabric.

senses.definition: not resulting from or achieved through deliberate planning
senses.example: An inadvertent click deleted the whole folder.

senses.definition: wanting to avoid activity or exertion; lazy
senses.example: The indolent cat slept in the sun all afternoon.

senses.definition: failing to take proper care in doing something
senses.example: The landlord was found negligent for ignoring the broken stairs.

senses.definition: feeling or appearing casually calm and relaxed; not displaying anxiety or interest
senses.example: He gave a nonchalant shrug, as if the prize meant nothing.

senses.definition: prejudiced in favor of a particular cause
senses.example: The debate turned into a partisan shouting match.

senses.definition: a strong supporter of a party, cause or person
senses.example: Partisans of both candidates filled the hall.

senses.definition: the presence of something in only small or insufficient quantities
senses.example: The paucity of evidence made a conviction unlikely.

senses.definition: excessively concerned with minor details or rules
senses.example: His pedantic corrections of everyone's grammar annoyed his friends.

senses.definition: a strong or habitual liking for something or tendency to do something
senses.example: She has a penchant for old maps.

senses.definition: to prevent from happening; to make impossible
senses.example: His injury precluded him from playing in the final.

senses.definition: to speak or act in an evasive way
senses.example: When asked about the missing funds, the treasurer prevaricated.

senses.definition: to restore friendly relations between
senses.example: The brothers were finally reconciled after years apart.

senses.definition: to make two apparently conflicting things compatible
senses.example: It is hard to reconcile his words with his actions.

senses.definition: deserving censure or condemnation
senses.example: Bullying a younger child is reprehensible.

senses.definition: to refuse to accept or be associated with
senses.example: The party repudiated the candidate's remarks.

senses.definition: to revoke, cancel or repeal a law, order or agreement
senses.example: The council rescinded the ban after a public outcry.

senses.definition: characterized by showing interest or concern
senses.example: The nurse was solicitous of her patients' comfort.

senses.definition: (of water or air) having no current or flow and often having an unpleasant smell as a consequence
senses.example: Mosquitoes breed in stagnant pools.

senses.definition: showing no activity; dull and sluggish
senses.example: Wages have been stagnant for a decade.

senses.definition: enduring pain and hardship without showing feelings or complaining
senses.example: She remained stoic throughout the long recovery.

senses.definition: a person who can endure pain or hardship without complaining
senses.example: A true stoic, he never mentioned the pain.

senses.definition: loud and harsh; grating
senses.example: The strident sound of the alarm woke the whole street.

senses.definition: presenting a point of view, especially a controversial one, in an excessively forceful way
senses.example: Her strident criticism of the plan alienated potential allies.

senses.definition: existing or occurring at or on the surface
senses.example: The cut was only superficial.

senses.definition: not thorough, deep or complete; cursory
senses.example: The report gave only a superficial account of the problem.

senses.definition: a state of physical or mental inactivity; lethargy
senses.example: The summer heat left the town in a kind of torpor.

senses.definition: present, appearing or found everywhere
senses.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous.
